description: Whether a remote turn is active, the remote-mode input to the working light (DESIGN v1.10 per-session remote turn tracking, v2.2 §B remote session focus). The turn table maps a session id (or "unknown-session" when a hook carried none) to the last sign of life; it is given here as ages in seconds before now. First the table is pruned: an entry survives only while it is strictly younger than the expiry (an entry exactly expirySeconds old is dropped). Then the turn is active when any surviving entry exists, or, with a focus set, only when the focused session has a surviving entry. Expected gives the surviving session ids sorted, and the active flag.
function: AppState.liveRemoteTurns(_:now:expiry:) then AppState.remoteTurnIsActive(_:focus:) — input {turnAgesSeconds, focus, expirySeconds} in, {kept, active} out
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.10 addendum (per-session turns, 15 minute expiry) and v2.2 §B (with a focus set, 'only its turn drives remoteTurnActive'), plus characterization of the Swift implementation (spec #94, ticket #125); Tests/PowerUpTests/StatusDerivationTests.swift. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/status.rs remote_turn_cases runs status::live_remote_turns then status::remote_turn_is_active, with ages as seconds before a fixed now.

cases.name: no turns
cases.reason: No session is mid-turn: the light rests.

cases.name: one fresh turn
cases.reason: A prompt was just submitted in a hooked session: amber.

cases.name: turn just under the expiry survives
cases.reason: A long turn with a recent enough sign of life stays active.

cases.name: turn exactly at the expiry is dropped
cases.reason: The cutoff is strict (last sign of life must be newer than now minus expiry); pins the boundary so a port cannot drift by one.

cases.name: turn past the expiry is dropped
cases.reason: The stuck-amber fix: a session killed mid-turn never sends Stop, so its entry must expire instead of pinning the light forever.

cases.name: expired turn dropped, fresh one kept
cases.reason: Pruning is per session: one dead session does not clear a live one, and a live one does not keep a dead one.

cases.name: two live sessions
cases.reason: Concurrent sessions each keep their own entry, the reason the single global flag was replaced.

cases.name: hook without a session id
cases.reason: Hooks that carry no session id are tracked under the shared unknown-session key and still light the bar.

cases.name: focused session is working
cases.reason: With a focus set, the focused session's turn drives the working light.

cases.name: only an unfocused session is working
cases.reason: With a focus set, other sessions still log but never turn the light amber; their entries are kept so clearing the focus shows them again.

cases.name: focused session expired, unfocused one live
cases.reason: Expiry applies to the focused session too, and an unfocused live session still does not count.

cases.name: focus set, no turns
cases.reason: A focus with nothing running rests.

cases.name: timestamp in the future is kept
cases.reason: Characterization: a last-seen time slightly ahead of now (clock adjustment) is younger than the cutoff, so it is kept rather than treated as dead.
